(Scch-23) Dated This The 2nd Day Of June - 2025 Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani B.Com. Ll.B (Spl) Xxi Addl. Scj & Acjm Member - Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc. No.2640/2024 Petitioner : Sri. texts.facts: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. 2. The facts leading to the filing of the instant petition are that on 30.03.2024 at about 2.30 a.m., when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-41-R-4810 along with pillion rider on the extreme left side of B.B.Road in slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Sanjeeviningar, Kodegehalli Flyover, Bengaluru City, the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA- 7363 which was moving ahead of the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, without giving any signal or indicator suddenly applied break, as a consequence of which the motorcycle dashed against car and fell down along with the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries. It is further urged that the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru wherein first aid treatment was provided and then he was shifted to St.John's Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and underwent several examinations and was discharged with an advice to take complete bed rest and regular followup treatment. He spent substantial amount towards his treatment. Further at the time of accident she was hale and healthy and he was brilliant student studying Bachelor of Physiotherepy course. Due to the accident he cannot concentrate on his studies and in future the petitioner cannot participate in any co-curricular activities. It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent manner of driving of the aforesaid car by its driver. The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount. 3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal. Hence he placed exparte. 4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts. This respondent denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363. However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy. Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act. This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident. Further it is contended that the alleged accident was happened due to the self negligence of the rider of the motorcycle and caused this accident, hence there is no negligence on the part of the driver of car. Further the rider of the motorcycle was driving the vehicle rash and negligent manner and failed to abide traffic rules, thus , is sole responsible for the accident. The petitioner himself riding the motorcycle and he being third party being a tortfeasor as such is not entitled to claim compensation in the matter. The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary party. Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the offending car and rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident. On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him. Further denied all the allegation made in the petition. Hence prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed : Mohammed Ashique R Allias Muhammed ... vs Roopa Murthy on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69234192/ 2 ISSUES 1) 6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1. Ex's .P1 to 25, Ex.P.37 & 38 were marked on his behalf. The MRO of Manipal Hospital was examined as PW.2. Ex.P.26 to 30 were marked through him. Further the MRO at St.Johns Hospital was examined as PW.3, through him Ex.P.31 to 34 got marked. Dr.Nagaraj. B.N, Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW.4. Ex's .P35 & 36 were marked through him. The respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.
texts.arguments: 14. It is relevant to relying on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court reported in 2020 0 Supreme(Kar) 104 (Shri Mallikarjun S/o. Yallappa Jogannavar and Ors. vs. Shri Umesh M. S/o. Murthy K. and Ors.) wherein the deceased in the above cited decision was an engineering student and the Hon'ble Court had considered his income at Rs.25,000/- p.m. and granted compensation. Further in the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in (2015) 2 SCC 180 (Ashwinbhai Jayantilal Modi vs. Ramkaran Ramachandra Sharma and another) wherein for a MBBS student, the Court has taken the income as Rs.25,000/- p.m. 18. The learned counsel for petitioner rendered the decisions : 1) (2018) 4 SCC 571 in the case of Jagdish V/s Mohan and others 2) 2005 ACJ 644 in the case of M.V Chowdappa V/s Mohan Breweries and Distilleries Ltd and another 3) 2011 ACJ 1971 in the case of B. Kothandapani V/s Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation Ltd., 4) 2011 ACJ 1 in the case of Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar and another (2011 (1) SCC 343) I have gone through the decisions. When such is the case physical disability assessed by the medical expert is on the higher side. All injuries and assessment of disability do not impact the earning capacity, nor in a similar way. The disability has to be seen in the context of the particular occupation or calling that the victim is engaged in. The co-relation between the physical disability suffered in an accident and the loss of earning capacity resulting from it was considered in great detail by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar V/s Ajaykumar and another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343. In the said case, the Apex Court held that it is the functional disability which would be the operative criteria for assessing the loss of future earnings and not the physical disability. Therefore compensation for loss of future earning has to be just & proper so as to enable him to live a life of dignity. 19. The point that merits consideration is that as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar V/s Ajaykumar, the doctor who treated an injured claimant or who has subsequently assessed his extent of permanent disability can give evidence only in regard to the extent of permanent disability.
